rule_link.how_it_backs: Justifies scoring the trunk_lean zone against the injured-runner pattern: injured runners show more forward trunk lean at midstance (with greater pelvic drop and a more extended knee at contact), so the rule flags excessive lean-plus-drop as the pathological cluster and cues tall, level running.

summary: Bramah and colleagues compared 3D running kinematics between runners with common soft-tissue injuries and healthy controls to look for a shared pathological gait. Injured runners showed greater contralateral pelvic drop, more forward trunk lean at midstance, and a more extended knee with more ankle dorsiflexion at initial contact. The authors conclude these patterns together may define a pathological running gait that cuts across specific injury diagnoses.
methods_signal: Case-control 3D kinematic comparison of runners with common soft-tissue running injuries versus uninjured controls, testing group differences across stance-phase trunk, pelvis, knee and ankle variables.

snippet.text: Injured runners share a look: dropped pelvis, extra trunk lean at midstance, straight knee at landing. If your photo shows that cluster, that is the first thing to fix.
